summary.intent: Assess and plan Phase 72 (SDK write-plane durability/correctness), clean up drifted todos across Phases 70-73, then execute a full plan→execute→ship cycle for Phase 72 while triaging two CI regressions (web-e2e, desktop-e2e) and subsequent test flakiness discovered along the way.
summary.outcome: Phase 71 CI regressions were root-caused and fixed (PR #601 merged: FUSE seq-1 equivocation fix, stale DTO driver, greptile perf opt; PR #600 merged: rotation-floor test fix, sdk-e2e Test 21 idempotency fix, 4 web-e2e flake fixes). Phase 72 was fully planned, executed across 10 plans + hardening work (vitest v3 test-drift fix, CI typecheck gate, cycle-guard DoS fix), verified, and PR #602 opened with all CI green; a HIGH-severity moveItem write-chain resurrection bug found by security review was fixed pre-merge, and CodeRabbit CLI triage/fixes were in progress when the transcript ends.

repo: Repo closes todos by deleting from pending/ and copying to completed/ (git mv), not moving to a 'resolved/' folder
gh workflow_dispatch on ci-e2e.yml only accepts `--ref <branch>` (checks out that branch's head), NOT `-f ref=<branch>` — the workflow definition predates the ref input
ci-e2e.yml (Web E2E + Desktop E2E) triggers ONLY on push-to-main or workflow_dispatch, never on PRs — PR-level e2e coverage requires manual dispatch against the branch before merge

Playwright web-e2e ciFloor() helper raises wait timeouts to 60s only under CI=1; locally waits stay at their literal (often 15-30s) value, causing IPNS-gated ops (deletes/creates/batch-ops) to flake locally on a cold or loaded stack even though they'd pass in CI

playwright.config.ts webServer.reuseExistingServer is `!process.env.CI`, so setting CI=1 locally to get the 60s floor also disables server reuse and conflicts with an already-running dev stack — must temporarily patch reuseExistingServer to test under the CI timeout regime locally
vitest does not load .env — test harnesses (e.g. sdk-e2e) that read process.env.SDK_E2E_SECRET fall back to a default fake secret unless the var is explicitly exported before running vitest

Restarting the local API from source (`nest start --watch` / rebuilding dist) is required to pick up current .env secrets — a stale running process silently serves old secrets causing 401s that look like config drift

Root tsconfig.json includes test files but tsconfig.build.json excludes them; CI's pnpm typecheck previously only ran build-based tsconfig, so test-file TypeScript errors never surfaced in CI despite existing

@cipherbox/* packages resolve cross-package types via workspace-symlinked dist (no path aliases/project references), so a package's test-inclusive typecheck must run after that package's dependencies are built — build-first then typecheck was chosen as the wiring order

Phase 71 (#599) shipped with three untracked pieces of test/fixture drift it never fixed: stale desktop-e2e .mts DTO field names, a flaky sdk-e2e idempotency assertion, and it exposed a latent FUSE seq-1 equivocation bug

GSD executor commits use non-conventional `feat 51-03:`/`refactor sdk:` style (no scope parens) which fails commitlint/pr-release-preview gates — must reword via git filter-branch before opening a PR (git rebase -i unavailable in this environment)
gh pr edit fails on this repo due to Projects-classic GraphQL incompatibility; PR body updates must go through `gh api -X PATCH .../pulls/<N> -F body=@file`

code.finding: publish_file_node hardcoded seq=1 on the first-publish branch gated only by 'inode cid empty', so a dropped/stale UploadComplete re-triggering that branch re-sealed at seq=1 with a new CID, tripping Phase 71's anti-equivocation gate; fixed by resolving IPNS first and routing Found-state into the existing CAS retry path

publish_with_cas_retry gained an optional preresolved_seq param (threaded from the caller's already-resolved sequence) to avoid a redundant second IPNS resolve on the Found path; conflict-retry path still always re-resolves since a pre-resolved value is stale after a conflict

getWriteBodyParams unified into a single shared implementation (previously duplicated in client.ts and bin/index.ts); zero/absent-writeKey short-circuit happens before the fail-closed resolve-and-throw branch so read-only fallback is preserved

Base-aware CAS-merge added: when baseWriteChildren is passed, a childId present in base but absent locally is pruned even if a racing writer's stale remote snapshot still carries it — prevents deleted WriteChildRefs from being resurrected on 409 retry. Falls back to a naive union (remote always wins) when baseWriteChildren is undefined

moveItem's source-folder publish dropped the moved child's WriteChildRef but never passed baseWriteChildren to updateFolderMetadataAndPublish, leaving it on the naive-union merge path — a concurrent stale republish of the source folder could resurrect the moved item's write link there (same resurrection class as the deleteItem bug SC#1 fixed). Found by security review, fixed by capturing sourceBaseWriteChildren before the filter and threading it through (commits dd8264a06/65024c3ce)

collectDescendantIpnsNames lacked the visited:Set<string> cycle guard that its sibling dfsFindFolder already had, allowing unbounded recursion (DoS/hang) on a cyclic or malicious folder graph; fixed by threading the same guard through all three call sites

workflow: When a background subagent's task-notification fires, read its full result before acting rather than assuming completion status from the summary line alone

Local reproduction of CI-only flakes should match the CI timeout regime (e.g. temporarily set CI=1 or patch webServer.reuseExistingServer) rather than chasing individual tests that surface in sequence as each earlier one is fixed — otherwise verification whack-a-moles through the whole suite
When two fixes touch overlapping CI legs (e.g. sdk-e2e), consolidate the fix onto one PR branch rather than spreading across separate branches to avoid duplicate-commit merge conflicts
Capture newly-discovered but out-of-scope work as a durable todo file immediately (before it's lost to context) rather than deferring it to memory

Sequencing a mechanical hardening pass (e.g. fixing all pre-existing test-type-drift) as the LAST plan in a phase covers both pre-existing drift and every new file the phase itself created, avoiding rework each wave

Security/crypto-sensitive phases benefit from a dedicated security-reviewer agent pass in parallel with CodeRabbit CLI before shipping — the security reviewer caught a HIGH finding (moveItem resurrection) that CodeRabbit's automated pass did not surface
